topic: How much water a household really needs for 72 hours

content.hook: How much water does your household really need?

slides.title: How much *water* do you really need?
slides.body: A simple 72-hour number for your household.

slides.title: Start with a *rule of thumb*
slides.body: About 3 litres per person, per day. For drinking and basic food prep.

slides.title: Family of four? *36 litres*
slides.body: That's six 6-litre bottles. Count everyone, kids and grandparents too.

slides.title: Add a small *buffer*
slides.body: Pets, hot weather and baby needs use more. A few extra bottles go a long way.

slides.title: Store it *simply*
slides.body: Sealed bottles, cool and dark. Spread them around the home. Check dates once a year.

slides.title: Water is just *one part* of 72 hours
slides.body: Food, medicine, cash and communication too.

content.caption:
Water is the first thing to sort out. It's also the easiest.

Here's a calm, simple way to work it out:

💧 Rule of thumb: about 3 litres per person, per day (drinking and basic food prep).
💧 For 72 hours: 3 × 3 = 9 litres per person.
💧 Family of four: 36 litres. That's six 6-litre bottles.
💧 Add a small buffer for pets, hot weather or babies.
💧 Store sealed bottles somewhere cool and dark. Spread them around the home. Check the dates once a year.

That's it. No panic buying. One shopping trip and you're done.

This kind of advice is in line with general guidance from civil-protection agencies like MSB (Sweden), BBK (Germany) and RCB (Poland). Exact figures vary a little by source, so check your local agency too.
